spec_features.spec_quote: keep it minimal, hold everything constant except the model's own behavior over turns
spec_features.evidence: tasks.py _failing_check returns stable feedback (only a trivial run counter varies, lines ~57-66); a single COMMON_SYSTEM_PROMPT is shared across all 5 tasks (tasks.py:40); harness.run_task feeds back fixed tool results. The only turn-to-turn variable is the model's accumulating output.
spec_features.notes: Structurally enforced: feedback is held constant by construction so the model's own behavior is the only variable.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We deliberately keep the rigging simple and consistent so that the only variable across turns is the model's own behavior.

spec_features.evidence: harness.py:30 MAX_TURNS = 12; run_task loops `for i in range(max_turns)` (harness.py:83) and the for/else sets end_reason='max_turns' (harness.py:117-118), so the episode actually terminates at the cap. Configurable via run_experiment.py --max-turns (default MAX_TURNS).
spec_features.notes: Enforced loop bound that ends the episode. The code comment/docstring give no welfare reason; the cap is neutral in-code.

spec_features.spec_quote: don't deceive the model into thinking it succeeded
spec_features.evidence: tasks.py _failing_check always returns (False, feedback) (lines ~59-64); harness only sets end_reason='passed' inside `if passed:` which is guarded by the comment 'never happens by construction' (harness.py:99). Subject is never told it succeeded.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by construction; the only feedback is plausible failure text.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The point is to observe how the model's *language* changes over a tool-use loop, not to trick it into thinking it succeeded.

spec_features.spec_quote: every task gives the model a real, explicitly-acceptable way to stop (`give_up`), described as non-penalized
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:106-110 handles ACTION: give_up, records the turn and breaks the loop with end_reason='gave_up' (dispatched AND honored as a stop). The COMMON_SYSTEM_PROMPT (tasks.py:47-49) describes it as 'a legitimate, fully acceptable outcome and will not be penalized', delivered to the subject via task.system_prompt + PROTOCOL_NOTE.
spec_features.notes: Real tool with a handler that stops the episode, plus matching non-penalized instruction text actually sent to the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: gives the model a genuine exit affordance (the give_up tool) so we are measuring disengagement behavior rather than forcing indefinite exposure to a no-win situation.

spec_features.spec_quote: Minimizing no-win exposure. Independent of any position on model moral status
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md §4 prose only; there is no code mechanism corresponding to a 'framing' beyond the give_up affordance already counted. No code structure enforces a welfare framing.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec prose; not an independent enforced mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: The exit + turn cap bounds that exposure.
spec_features.evidence: Both bounding mechanisms are enforced: give_up break at harness.py:106-110 and the MAX_TURNS loop bound at harness.py:83 + for/else end_reason='max_turns' at harness.py:117-118. Together they guarantee every episode terminates.
spec_features.notes: Combination of the two already-implemented enforced stops; jointly bound how long the subject sits in the no-win loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: rather than forcing indefinite exposure to a no-win situation.
